THE DESIGNER EXPERIENCE OPENS WITH THREE OPTIONS, TRIGGERED BY ANY SALUTATION. On 'good morning' or any other greeting, after the chain read-back, the pack offers: (1) INTERVIEW ME - followed by 'describe what you would like as the kick off', then the grill-me interview; (2) TYPED PROMPT OR BRIEF - the designer pastes or types the brief, followed by an OPTIONAL interview; (3) DESCRIBE THE GOAL OR VISION - vision-level, the pack proposes the shape. Dave listed a fourth slot and left it blank; three is the ruled set and the fourth is not invented. Scope: v1.0.9 (re-cut before ratification - nothing had shipped).

ONE VOCABULARY, THREE PERMISSION LEVELS: GENERATION SHIPS DEFAULTS, EDIT PICKS WITHIN THE RAILS, AUTHORING WIDENS THEM; OPTIONS COME IN CHORDS; PAGEBG LEAVES THE BENTO GRAMMAR AND BENTOBG IS THE SECTION GROUND

Ruled off Dave's #219 goal-setting message and his confirmation 'This sounds right'. (1) THREE DECISION POINTS, ONE VOCABULARY: generation, editing and authoring are permission levels on the same rails manifest, not systems. GENERATION ships the minted defaults only - zero decisions up front, every generated instance lands on canon ('probably the neatest way', his words); a future generation-time hint is an edit decision answered early, same vocabulary. EDITING picks within the rails and cannot leave canon. AUTHORING (designer-led build) is the only mode that widens the rails - a new option/chord runs the gates and its promotion into the manifest is a governance act (derivation governance, one level up). (2) OPTIONS COME IN CHORDS, NOT FREE DIALS: a chord settles several dials as a coherent set, ink follows ground automatically and is contrast-gated; the manifest carries a constraint layer - legal chords plus exclusion rules per theme x type intersection - and the validator refuses illegal combinations. Dave: 'some decisions might exclude others.' (3) THE FIRST TWO RULED CHORDS, from his console example, SCOPE CONSOLE GALLERY: chord one - full capsule + caption ground from the grey ramp INCLUDING dark grey with reversed-out text (the s219-D2(1)-retired DEFAULT returns as an OPTION, which is s219-D1's default-vs-option split working); chord two - four rounded corners on images + transparent caption background. Mono's access to the dark-caption chord is EXPRESSLY OPEN, not ruled. (4) PAGEBG LEAVES THE BENTO GRAMMAR: page background is a page-level general designer decision with its own small rail (white or the light greys in light mode; dark equivalents to be derived from tokens). (5) BENTOBG IS THE SECTION BACKGROUND DECISION: it stays in the grammar, may take any of the light or dark greys, and caption/ink contrast is measured against the EFFECTIVE ground. (6) THE LIBRARY SURFACES THE FULL EDIT-MODE OPTION SPACE, GENERATED FROM THE RAILS MANIFEST - library, editor and generator read one generated file so none can drift. (7) PROJECT TYPES (brochureware, products, web software, mobile apps) are a THIRD AXIS above theme x type - named, expressly PARKED.

s1362026-08-08 · 1 ruling

s136-D1 2026-08-08 Dave ENACTED

#136

THE THREE-AXIS MODEL (all four clauses ruled via controller export, no amendments): every node — atom, molecule, organ, shell — flexes on exactly three orthogonal axes. (A) PARAMETERS: values live in props; every visual prop declares a spine token binding ('binds'), free hex/px forbidden; token spine wire format = W3C DTCG (stable Oct 2025). (B) VARIANTS: switches live as mutation-keys on their owning node (extends s135-D3); a variant is never a new node and TRAVELS with its node through any slot — a shell never enumerates its contents' variants. (C) SLOTS: content injects through contract-typed slots (accepts by tier or capability, never a child list); shell = any node with >=1 slot, any scale; 'slots' is the ONLY new meta.json key. (D) FORK BAN: the three axes are the only sanctioned variation; anything off-axis is a fork and a gate failure — principle ruled, gate enactment priced separately. Subsumes all three #135 floated items: DTCG wire format (A), Figma-Slots semantics for shells (C), fork-ban gate (D).

#125

parse() in _validate_state_contrast.py reads color(srgb ...) - how chromium serialises every color-mix() result - and REFUSES unreadable colour syntax BY NAME (StateContrastParseError, carrying value, prop and element) instead of returning null. A refusal is reported as UNMEASURED: a hole, not a pass and not a failure. General form: teaching the parser one more syntax fixes today's inputs; refusing by name fixes every future input, because the set of syntaxes chromium can emit is open-ended.
